articles.headline: 2026 NFL trade deadline updates: Jordan Davis, Andre Cisco on the move
articles.description: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. We're following all the action, including Jessie Bates III, Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis to the Jaguars.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NFLトレード期限の最新情報：ジョーダン・デイビスとアンドレ・シスコが移籍
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのトレード期限は東部時間火曜日の午後4時です。ジェシー・ベイツ3世、ダヴォン・ゴドホー、ジョーダン・デイビスのジャガーズへの移籍を含む、あらゆる動きを追っています。
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. We already have seen plenty of deals -- and more are on the way.

On Monday, the Jaguars traded for safety Jessie Bates III, defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and defensive tackle Jordan Davis. The Lions also added safety help with Andre Cisco.

Other big names to be dealt so far include Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, J.J. McCarthy to the Giants, Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens and Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys.

We're tracking all in-season moves and trade-related buzz right through the deadline. The most recent deals will be added at the top.

More coverage:

Transactions | Depth charts

Grading every big trade

Tracking deals, intel over final two days

Nov. 4

Cardinals trade QB Brissett to Ravens

Ravens get: QB Jacoby Brissett, 2027 fifth-round pick

Cardinals get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 seventh-round pick

The Cardinals finalized a trade to send QB Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens on Friday. The Cardinals are sending a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-rounder in exchange for Brissett and a 2027 fourth-round selection.

Brissett's first start as the Ravens' starting quarterback could come as soon as Week 10 when Baltimore hosts the Chargers on "Monday Night Football." He was recently benched by the Cardinals before the trade.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides

Hensley: Can Brissett save the Ravens?

Oct. 29

Titans trade DT Simmons to Bears

Bears get: DT Jeffery Simmons, 2028 fifth-round pick

Titans get: 2027 first-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 first-round pick

The Bears are acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The Titans are receiving 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, plus a 2027 fourth-round pick from the Bears in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick, the sources told Schefter.

Simmons, 29, signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension with $100 million guaranteed with the Titans in June. He is under contract through the 2030 season.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides

Staff: Answering big questions on the deal

Barnwell: Does trading two first-rounders work?

Oct. 27

Colts trade DT Buckner to 49ers

49ers get: DT DeForest Buckner

Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick

The Colts are trading three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the 49ers, the team that made him a 2016 first-round pick before dealing him to Indianapolis in 2020, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

The Colts will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from the 49ers, sources said.

Wagoner: Are the 49ers stopping at Buckner?

Seahawks get: G Quenton Nelson

articles.headline: Are Jaguars all-in after trades for Bates, Davis? Plus Eagles, Falcons reaction
articles.description: Jacksonville made a trio of trades Monday. What it means for Eagles and Falcons ... and the Jaguars' Super Bowl hopes.
articles.headlineJa: ベイツとデイビスの獲得で、ジャガーズは勝負に出たのか？イーグルスとファルコンズの反応も
articles.descriptionJa: ジャクソンビルは月曜日に3件のトレードを行いました。これがイーグルスやファルコンズにどのような影響を与えるのか、そしてジャガーズのスーパーボウル制覇への望みについて。
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars addressed two of their biggest weaknesses ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline by acquiring safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and defensive tackle Jordan Davis from the Philadelphia Eagles.

Jacksonville gave up a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick for Bates and a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for Davis. The Jaguars also traded a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick for New Orleans Saints DT Davon Godchaux, who will provide depth. 

At 6-2, the Jaguars are in third place in the AFC and have a three-game lead in the AFC South. These moves could suggest a win-now mentality.

Bates, who made the Pro Bowl in 2023, can stabilize a secondary that has been hit with multiple injuries at safety and cornerback. The Jaguars made a similar move last season at the trade deadline by acquiring receiver Jakobi Meyers to help a position group that had multiple players out with injuries, and that keyed an offensive surge that carried them to a division title. The hope is that Bates can do the same for the secondary because getting through the AFC means beating some of the league's top quarterbacks -- especially Buffalo's Josh Allen.

The Falcons, on the other hand, were able to get good draft capital for a player on an expiring contract but are still competing in the NFC South.

For the Jaguars, adding Davis and Godchaux secures a defensive front that lost nose tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the season with a quad injury.

Davis is coming off a career year in 2025 which he posted highs in sacks (4.5), tackles for loss (nine), quarterback hits (six), tackles (72) and passes defensed (six), helping him land a three-year, $78 million contract extension in March.

The Eagles, who have traded away multiple players this year, seem to be retooling for the future.

What does this move mean for the Jaguars' defense, the Eagles' future and the Falcons' draft plans? ESPN NFL Nation reporters Michael DiRocco, Marc Raimondi and Tim McManus and NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid take a look at how the trades impact each team.

Jump to a team:

Are the Jaguars going all-in after acquiring Jordan Davis?

It absolutely seems that way.

According to DraftKings, Jacksonville is now third in Super Bowl odds (moved from +850 to +750 after the trades) behind the 49ers (+540) and Bills (+650).

articles.headline: A 'confident' C.J. Stroud soaks in five-TD day against Chargers
articles.description: Stroud matched his career high with 5 TD passes and added 384 passing yards in the win.
articles.headlineJa: チャージャーズ戦で5TDを記録、自信に満ちたC.J.ストラウドが快挙を噛みしめる
articles.descriptionJa: ストラウドは勝利の中で5つのパスによるタッチダウンを決め、キャリアハイとなる384パスヤードを記録しました。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Sunday's five-touchdown performance from C.J. Stroud against the Los Angeles Chargers punctuated a hot start for the Houston Texans quarterback.

Stroud & Co. were dominant in their 44-22 win, as he tied a career high in touchdowns to go with 384 yards passing, tied for his second most in a game. Week 9's performance was something Stroud promised himself to "enjoy" -- rather than immediately moving on.

"I beat myself up a lot when I don't do great, so I'm going to enjoy this and celebrate with my friends, family and teammates because I know what it feels like to throw a couple interceptions," Stroud said. "So, you need to be positive towards yourself. Something that playing the quarterback position has taught me about life, is that everyone could view you one way, but all that matters is how God views you and how you view yourself, so I'm grateful that God has allowed me to have some tough skin and be able to push through some tough times.

"Days like this come from being on the other side when you're not playing so great."

The Texans might be 3-5, but it's not been because of poor quarterback play. Through eight games, it's the strongest start Stroud has had to a season. He has completed 64.2% of his throws for 2,251 yards, 16 touchdowns with only two interceptions, while posting a 104.8 passer rating, and he's currently on pace for career highs in passing yards and touchdowns.

Coach DeMeco Ryans said the fuel for Stroud's high-level performance is "confidence."

"You see the growth, you see the maturity in C.J.," Ryans said. "He's a top quarterback in his league because of that, because of his steadiness in the pocket, his resolve, his great energy all day. And he's having a phenomenal year, phenomenal year, and he's definitely deserving of all the recognition that he should get."

Against the Chargers, Stroud spread the ball around to all of his playmakers -- with receivers Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell going over 100 yards.

Dell finished with 105 yards and a touchdown in only his second game since missing 25 straight after sustaining multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in December of 2024. 

Boutte, who Houston acquired during the late stages of training camp, had 125 receiving yards with two touchdowns, marking his first 100-yard outing of the season.

"It's fun to watch, fun to watch him spin it," Ryans said. "He's thrown it to a lot of different people, which is what I'm most proud of. Everybody's getting the touch, and the guys are showing up and capitalizing on the opportunities that they do get."

The Texans' offense now ranks 11th in yards (356.5) and ninth in points per game (26.1), and a majority of that production is from their quarterback -- who's now back to playing the way he was during his historic rookie season in 2023.

articles.headline: Dianna Russini returning to sports media with show, column for BetUS
articles.description: Dianna Russini is returning to sports media with a new weekly football show and column for the Costa Rica-based gambling company BetUS.
articles.headlineJa: ダイアナ・ルシニ、BetUSでの番組とコラムでスポーツメディアに復帰
articles.descriptionJa: ダイアナ・ルシニは、コスタリカを拠点とするギャンブル企業BetUSでの新しい週刊フットボール番組とコラムを通じて、スポーツメディアに復帰します。
articles.body:
Dianna Russini is returning to sports media.

Russini, the former Athletic and ESPN NFL reporter, will launch a new weekly football show and write a column with her league insights for the Costa Rica-based gambling company BetUS.

Russini's BetUS show will debut Wednesday, marking her first media venture since April, when she resigned from The Athletic after the New York Post published photographs showing her and New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel hugging and holding hands at an adults-only Arizona resort.

The Athletic published a report over the summer that found Russini violated company policy by not disclosing her relationship with Vrabel, but that it had little effect on her coverage.

Russini told People Magazine on Monday that navigating the media firestorm after the photos were first published was difficult but that the NFL community of players and executives was a source of support.

"The absolute best part of this situation has been the loyalty the NFL has shown me," Russini said.

She said players checked on her often and encouraged her to return to covering the league, adding, "They became sort of the people that I was learning from during this."

Her new show, "The Russini Report," will include gambling analysis and weekly game previews, including commentary from NFL experts. Super Bowl champion coach Bill Parcells and sports radio personality Damon Amendolara will be Russini's first guests.

BetUS streams content on its website and on the social media platform X.

Russini will also appear on the podcast of sports media personality Jon Weiner, better known as Stugotz, to deliver NFL analysis.

Before The Athletic, Russini worked as an NFL reporter for ESPN.

articles.headline: Sources: Man United turn to U.S. coach Pochettino with Carrick on the brink
articles.description: United States coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favored candidate to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：キャリックが解任寸前の中、マンUはポチェッティーノ監督に注目
articles.descriptionJa: 関係者がESPNに語ったところによると、アメリカ代表監督のマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノが、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの監督としてマイケル・キャリックの後任となる有力候補です。
articles.body:
United States coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favored candidate to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager with the club ready to fire the 45-year-old due to growing alarm over the team dropping into the Premier League relegation zone, sources have told ESPN.

The United hierarchy, led by co-chairman Joel Glazer, minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, is assessing Carrick's position after the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season left United just one point off the bottom of the table having won once in 10 league games to date.

- Ogden: Ratcliffe chose to appoint rookies at Man United, and it has them facing relegation﻿ fight

While sources have said discussions are ongoing and will continue over the coming days, they have also told ESPN that there is now acceptance that performances and results demand a change of manager.

Pochettino, 54, extended his contract with the U.S. Soccer Federation until 2030 in August after guiding the United States to the round of 16 at the World Cup this summer.

A source told ESPN that the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain coach has an escape clause in his contract with the U.S. for $10 million (£7.4 million), which Man United would have to pay for the Argentine's services.

Former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is another candidate admired by United bosses. Julian Nagelsmann, who is also currently out of work, is among the options, and Kieran McKenna, who was interviewed for the job in 2024, has supporters at Old Trafford.

But it is Pochettino -- who has interviewed for the United job on three previous occasions -- who is regarded as having the Premier League experience and personality needed to drag United out of danger and revive the club's fortunes.

Carrick signed a two-year contract at United in the summer after guiding the club to Champions League qualification following his arrival as interim manager in January.

Sources have said that United believed Carrick, whose only previous managerial experience was with Championship team Middlesbrough, merited a long-term deal after his success at Old Trafford last season.

But senior figures have been shocked by the drop in performances and results this season. After they gave the former United midfielder time to turn around the situation last month, Carrick has been able to win only one of four games since his reprieve, and sources have said that his prospects are now increasingly bleak.

United are next in action against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

- Neville on Carrick's Man United future: 'Ownership don't have a clue'

articles.headline: Schottenheimer: Cowboys will be without Ferguson, Goodson for 'multiple weeks'
articles.description: The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday, a day after his team posted a 27-23 victory against the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," according to coach Brian Schottenheimer.

According to sources, Ferguson suffered sprained posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligaments in his left knee in the third quarter of Sunday's 27-23 win against the Indianapolis Colts. Goodson suffered a knee injury in the second quarter but managed to return in the second half. He finished with 12 carries for a career-high 77 yards.

Ferguson, who is second on the team in touchdown catches (four), was hit awkwardly on an 11-yard catch and immediately grabbed at his knee. He remained on the sideline after getting the knee taped up but did not return.

"A lot of these guys, they play on adrenaline, and this is a guy that has been incredible for us really the last two weeks," Schottenheimer said of Goodson. "And these guys, they want to tough it out. They care. They want to win. They want to do whatever it takes. And just doing some more exams and scans and things like that, a few things showed up that we'll keep an eye for."

Complicating matters for the Cowboys is the fact they have just one slot remaining on their injured reserve/designated to return list, having put the designation on seven players. A player misses at least four games if he is placed on injured reserve/DTR.

"We're working through it," Schottenheimer said.

Tight end Luke Schoonmaker (groin) has missed the past two games, but he will be available this week to help alleviate Ferguson's absence, Schottenheimer said.

The Cowboys have only fullback Hunter Luepke on the 53-man roster behind Javonte Williams, but Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin are on the practice squad.

"There's a lot of different ways to do it," Schottenheimer said of the running back breakdowns. "I have a lot of confidence in Izzy. We'll be looking at a lot of different potential moves that we can make, but I'm not going to pretend that losing Goody doesn't affect us. The guy's been playing great football."

Wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder, hamstring), cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (back, hamstring) were inactive against the Colts, and Schottenheimer said they will follow a similar practice plan this week by being limited before a decision is made on their availability for the San Francisco 49ers.

Safety P.J. Locke has been ruled out for this week after suffering a concussion for the second straight week. Wide receiver Jonathan Mingo was unable to finish the Colts game and his status is uncertain. Wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) will work into practice this week but has missed the past three games.

"Busy week in the training room for us," Schottenheimer said.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic returns for Lakers; Austin Reaves, Quentin Grimes out vs. Hawks
articles.description: Luka Doncic returns for the Lakers on Monday at Atlanta, but the team will be without Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (sprained finger).
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- The Los Angeles Lakers will get Luka Doncic back in the lineup Monday against the Atlanta Hawks but will not be at full strength with Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (sprained finger on right hand) both out, the team announced.

Reaves scored a season-high 43 points in Sunday's 121-116 win over the Detroit Pistons while Doncic was sidelined because of lower back tightness.

Doncic will resume his scorching-hot start to the season, with his 361 points so far representing the third-most points through nine games in NBA history.

Doncic, who leads the league with a 40.1 points-per-game average, has scored 40-plus points in four straight games.

Lakers coach JJ Redick said that with Reaves and Grimes sidelined, he planned to give early rotation minutes to rookie Cameron Carr, L.A.'s first-round pick.

The Lakers came into Monday on a five-game winning streak, while the Hawks have won four straight.

articles.headline: Doc Rivers says he apologized to Giannis Antetokounmpo while clarifying critiques
articles.description: Doc Rivers said he reached out to apologize to Giannis Antetokounmpo for questioning his basketball IQ, saying he meant more that the force he plays with can get "in the way of his feel."
articles.body:
Former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers told ESPN Andscape on Monday that he reached out to Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo to apologize for a remark he made on a recent podcast.

Rivers, now an NBA analyst for NBC Sports, coached Antetokounmpo in Milwaukee for parts of three seasons before being relieved of his duties at the end of last season. Rivers told "The Bill Simmons Podcast" in an episode posted last Thursday that Antetokounmpo "doesn't necessarily have this super IQ" for basketball and that he "really has one way: downhill, force, force."

 

Rivers told ESPN Andscape he meant to say "feel for the game" instead of "super IQ," he felt bad about the error in words and texted Antetokounmpo an apology that the latter responded positively to.

"I was saying he was one of the most interesting guys," Rivers said. "He makes unbelievable passes, but at then at times because of his force he plays at it gets in the way of his feel. It was more of a compliment. I hate this and feel bad about it. I apologize for the distraction. I'm not trying to be one."

Rivers also said Antetokounmpo was "not easy" to coach during the podcast. The Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame coach told Andscape that those comment were actually meant as a compliment to his greatness, not as a slight. Rivers also added that he made a lot of positive comments on the podcast about Antetokounmpo, including enjoying coaching the former Bucks star, that were overlooked.

"The point was trying to make is whenever you have a great player, you have to fit the team around that great player," Rivers told ESPN Andscape. "That is the point I was trying to make. It's not always easy. It's a compliment. I've been successful and unsuccessful at it. But your job is to create the best team you can possibly create around that great player and his talents."

Antetokounmpo addressed Rivers' comments Sunday, three days after the interview was published. 

"First of all, he's not my coach," Antetokounmpo told reporters after Miami's 114-108 victory over the Sacramento Kings. "My coach is Coach Spo [Erik Spoelstra], but [Rivers] is a guy -- a coach -- that I've worked with in the past. I'm speechless."

Antetokounmpo, 31, is averaging 27.5 points and 12.8 rebounds in his first season with the Heat, who have rebounded from a slow start and improved to 4-6 with Sunday's victory in Sacramento.

articles.headline: Bronny James gets into verbal exchange with Pistons fans during Lakers' win
articles.description: Lakers guard Bronny James was captured getting into a verbal exchange with fans at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday night during L.A.'s win over the Pistons.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers guard Bronny James was captured getting into a verbal exchange with fans at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday night during the Lakers' 121-116 win against the Detroit Pistons.

James, the son of Philadelphia 76er LeBron James, was seen responding to heckling fans seated near the Lakers bench during a timeout before being rerouted by staff.

A video shared on social media shows James snapping back at the fans, asking if they could "run a mile" and "how much money" they made.

The video then shows the fans being spoken to by security before being removed from their seats for violating courtside policy.

It wasn't the only fan interaction of the night involving a Laker. Austin Reaves, who scored a season-high 43 points, had an exchange with another fan sitting courtside before halftime. Reaves hunched over and had an extended conversation with the Pistons fan before teammate Matisse Thybulle pulled him away.

Reaves later pointed and waved at the fan after hitting a late 3 to help put the game out of reach with 46 seconds remaining.

articles.headline: Monday's fantasy hoops adds, NBA bets to make: Ty Jerome primed for a big game
articles.description: Andre Snellings breaks down Monday's eight-game NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Monday

The NBA starts off this week with eight games on the docket, including three between two teams that both enter with winning records.

The first such matchup features the red-hot Los Angeles Lakers traveling to Atlanta to face the Hawks. The Lakers defeated the Detroit Pistons on Sunday even with Luka Doncic (back) sidelined, behind 43 points from Austin Reaves. Doncic is questionable to return for tonight's game.

The Memphis Grizzlies (6-3) head north of the border to face the Toronto Raptors (5-4). Memphis' Ty Jerome has scored more than 20 points in three straight games, his second such streak of the season, and will try to get to a fourth tonight.

And in Houston, two early-season MVP candidates lock horns when the Rockets (7-3) host the Denver Nuggets (5-3). The key to tonight's win might be which of Nikola Jokic and Kevin Durant are able to put on a more MVP-caliber performance.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and potential fantasy streamers, let's take a closer look at all of tonight's action.

Fantasy stream team

Players available in at least 50% of leagues

Jakob Poeltl, C, Toronto Raptors (rostered in 36.3% of ESPN basketball leagues)

Poeltl has been dealing with a shoulder injury that slowed his start to the season, but he had a breakout in his last outing that suggested he is on the road to recovery. On Friday, with Scottie Barnes (groin) sidelined, Poeltl dropped 19 points, 11 boards and 3 steals in 31 minutes. This marked his second double-double in his last three games played.

Saddiq Bey, SF/PF, New Orleans Pelicans (35.9%)

Bey is fully settled into his role as the shooting/scoring sixth man for the Pelicans. Even though he comes off the bench, in many games Bey becomes one of the primary scorer on the team when he is locked in. He often finishes halves, which keeps him playing near starter-minutes. In his last five games, Bey has averaged 19.8 PPG, 1.8 3PG and 1.4 SPG in 29.6 MPG.

P.J. Washington, PF/SF, Dallas Mavericks (36.8%)

Washington has started every game this season, notching double digits in either points or rebounds, or both, in nine of 10 games. He has scored 20 or more points in two of his last three games, including a 21-point/10-rebound game that marked his second 20-10 effort of the season.

Quenton Jackson, PG/SG, Indiana Pacers (5.0%)

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United to hire USMNT's Pochettino to replace Carrick?
articles.description: Manchester United are in the relegation zone and could turn to United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂とニュース：マン・ユナイテッドがキャリックの後任に米国代表のポチェッティーノを起用か？
articles.descriptionJa: 降格圏に位置するマンチェスター・ユナイテッドは、マイケル・キャリックの後任として米国代表のマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノ監督を招聘する可能性がある。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is the current favorite to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, while the club want to bolster their defense with the signing of Nottingham Forest defender Murillo. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are in the relegation zone and could turn to United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick, says The Standard. In August, Pochettino, who managed Tottenham and Chelsea in the Premier League, signed a new contract until 2030, which could complicate matters. But former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany, Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig boss Julian Nagelsmann, who are both free agents, are among the other managers also reported to be on United's shortlist.

- Football Insider reports that Man United want to bolster their defense with the signing of Nottingham Forest defender Murillo. The Brazil international, 24, joined from Corinthians in 2023 for around €6 million, but his transfer could be worth 10 times that now. United are also reported to be interested in Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri. The Red Devils were surprise suitors for the 25-year-old late in the summer, when it appeared an exit from City could be on the cards, and if they pull off a January deal it would be a rare cross-city move -- one that hasn't happened directly between the rivals since 2012.

- United have also been busy scouting other potential transfer targets in the market, according to Nicolò Schira, after attending a match between Atalanta and Monza. The club have been monitoring Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi, 26, who has a deal that expires in 2028, and Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with the 21-year-old being linked with a host of different clubs after scoring nine goals in 10 Serie A appearances.

- Fabrizio Romano has ruled out a potential move away from Inter Miami for Lionel Messi. The 39-year-old has recently been linked with a possible return to Newell's Old Boys in Argentina, one of the first teams he played for as an academy star, to see out his career. But with a contract that runs until 2028, Messi is set to stay in MLS for the next two years before considering his next possible options.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea are among a whole host of teams tracking the future of Lens defender Ismaelo Ganiou, according to TEAMtalk. The 21-year-old center back has been with the French club since last summer, making 37 senior appearances in that time as he continues to develop. That has caught the eye of the two London clubs, which are looking to invest in the backline for the future, while PSG, Manchester City, Newcastle, Fulham, and Brentford are also named as clubs that have been keeping an eye on Ganiou's progress.

articles.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders.

Nov. 9

Hoop Collective: Are the Lakers and Warriors legit contenders in the West?

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to cover surprising starts for several teams in the NBA, including the rejuvenated Golden State Warriors and the impressive Los Angeles Lakers. They then break down the latest Oklahoma City Thunder trade before closing on the first matchup between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers this season.

Topics: 

0:48: Early surprises of the NBA season

2:58: Do the Warriors need to be taken seriously?

15:36: What does Kristaps Porzingis' update mean for Warriors?

22:13: Lakers starting to look like a complete team

33:48: An interesting trade by the Thunder

49:45: First 76ers-Celtics matchup Tuesday

MacMahon on why the Thunder made the trade on Sunday: "First off, the Thunder need wings. So the the Thunder needed a wing and they needed to manage the payroll. And you know when we did the thing on the Thunder in the wake -- we didn't know at the time how long Chet was going to be out -- but in the wake of the injuries to Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams, we talked to people around the league about all the different ways that Thunder might address this.

"And we talked about how, hey, going after a guy like a Herb Jones or Trey Murphy, like don't hold your breath for the Thunder to take on a contract of those sizes because they're having to manage their payroll, which is why they traded three role players who helped them win a championship just a couple of years ago.

"This is a buy-low deal, just like it was with Jared McCain.

"... He's got this year plus two more left on his rookie contract, and next year, his salary is $3.4 million. So a year after that, it's five, five and change, like it's almost six. Look I don't know whether Nique Clifford will work out. But this is exactly the type of move that the Thunder specialize in."
